chunks: And Dāwūd ibn Sirḥān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

Regarding a man who wishes to marry off his sister, he said: "He should consult her. If she remains silent, then that is her consent; and if she refuses, he should not marry her off. If she says, 'Marry me to so-and-so,' then he should marry her to whomever she approves of. And the orphan girl in the care of a man, he should not marry her off except to one whom she is pleased with."

key_terms.تَرْضَى: she approves of or is pleased with
key_terms.سَكَتَتْ: she remained silent, indicating consent in this context
key_terms.فِي حِجْرِ الرَّجُلِ: under the care and guardianship of a man
key_terms.يُؤَامِرُهَا: he consults her and seeks her view regarding the marriage

ai.seo_question: Does a guardian need a woman’s consent before marrying her off in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a woman’s approval is required in marriage arrangements made by her guardian or relative. It specifically emphasizes consultation with one’s sister and the necessity of the orphan girl’s satisfaction when she is under a man’s care.
